name: 8q123d-vault-account-picker
goal: A vault request that names no account offers every saved entry for the same site, so a saved password is never asked for again

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Request 055deab2 (github automation-login): old app matches only entry.service == request.service and the live broker sends no site/account; a GitHub login saved under another name shows 'Vault item missing' and asks for the password again. Expected: offer every saved login for the site; Daniel picks; add only when none is saved.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: No standardized test covered account choice: credential-vault-ios.e2e covers signing and sealing only; the old app's matching lived in untested view model code. New native e2e compiles the Swift matcher and asserts outcomes for synthetic entries.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Test-only commit 226f5eee00: 7 of 8 fail; first: expected { offered: [], kind: 'missing' } to deeply equal { kind: 'choose' }.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: VaultAccountMatch + VaultAccountPickerSection in Vault/Picker/; broker queue site/account in dafuga/credential-broker PR #14.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: Unchanged test 8/8 passes at 400058b333 (loop record green).

steps.title: Run harness loop siblings to record the root cause and evaluate the same pattern across committed source.
Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
